seo_description: ClipRecallBar is a free, open-source clipboard history for the macOS menu bar. Press Shift-Command-V, type to filter, press Return to paste. No network.
hero_sub: ClipRecallBar keeps your copy history in the menu bar. Press ⇧⌘V, type to filter, and hit Return to paste into the app you were using.
features_sub: Everything is built around the keyboard, and your history never leaves your Mac.

features.title: Search, then paste on Return
features.desc: Filter as you type with case- and diacritic-insensitive matching, then use the arrow keys and Return. Option-Return pastes as plain text, and ⌘1 to ⌘9 paste a row directly.

features.title: Text, rich text, files, images
features.desc: Captures plain text, RTF, file URLs and images. Duplicates move to the top instead of piling up, and history size is adjustable from 20 to 999 entries.

features.title: Skips password manager copies
features.desc: Items marked concealed or transient are never stored. You can also ignore specific apps by bundle identifier or pause capture from the menu.

features.title: Pin what you reuse
features.desc: Press ⌘P to pin an entry. Pinned items sort to the top and survive Clear History.

features.title: Floating panel near your pointer
features.desc: A global hotkey opens a compact borderless panel with the search field already focused. The shortcut is configurable in Settings.

features.title: No network, local storage
features.desc: There are no accounts, servers or network code. History is saved as local files, with a corrupt file moved aside rather than crashing the app.

permissions_step: When prompted, grant Accessibility in System Settings › Privacy & Security so ClipRecallBar can send ⌘V to paste; without it, items are still copied and you press ⌘V yourself.

faq.q: Is ClipRecallBar really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license, with no accounts, subscriptions or ads. If it helps you, there is an optional Support / Donate button in the menu.

Accessibility, only to send the ⌘V keystroke that pastes into your previous app. If you decline, everything else works and a banner reminds you to press ⌘V. Launch at login is optional and may ask for approval under Login Items; it does not request Screen Recording or Microphone access.

faq.q: Where is my clipboard data stored?
faq.a: Only on your Mac, in ~/Library/Application Support/ClipRecallBar/. Text and metadata are saved as JSON and images as PNG files. The app makes no network connections.

Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, and this is a free open-source project. Right-click the app and choose Open once to run it, or build it yourself from source with Xcode and XcodeGen.
